Write B on the trend scale $X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t}$ with $T'(t)=\mu>0$. The question states constant autocovariance for the levels and a linear $10\%$ p.a. trend, i.e. the deviation $M_{t}$ is stationary around the trend, not an integrated martingale. On the random-walk-with-drift reading $E[M_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=M_{s}$ and $E[ \int M_{t}dq_{t}]=0$ for predictable $q$. On the trend-stationary reading the problem intends $E[M_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=\rho^{t-s}M_{s}$ with $|\rho|<1$, $E[M_{t}]=0$ and constant autocovariance, so the price level is not a sub-martingale pointwise: 
$E[X_{t+\Delta}\mid\mathcal F_{t}]=X_{t}+\mu\Delta+(\rho^{\Delta}-1)M_{t}$.

For a fixed calendar date $E[X_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}]$ so the two baskets share the same $10\%$ p.a. physical drift in first moment. The price levels are $10\%$ drift processes, not physical martingales, so the formal martingale prefaces in B,C,D are inaccurate for the level and $D$ is false. The return distribution is stationary in the drift-adjusted sense, $E[r_{t}]=10\%$.

Let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction still held, $h_{30}=1$, $h_{31}=0$. Cash is $C_{h}=\int X_{t}d(-h_{t})$. With $M$ stationary mean-reverting,
$E[\int M_{t}d(-h_{t})]$ can be made $>0$ by putting more sale weight on $M_{t}>0$ realisations. Mean reversion erodes a positive deviation: $E[M_{t+\Delta}\mid M_{t}>0]=\rho^{\Delta}M_{t}<M_{t}$. Hence a price-contingent rule that sells more when a new intra-year high is reached and holds when $M_{t}<0$ harvests the mean-reverting component. The loss of drift accrual from selling early can be more than compensated by the positive expected mean-reversion harvest.

Hence $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}X_{t}] > E[X_{31}]$ and the Snell envelope of a trend-stationary drifted process is strictly above the European payoff. An adapted liquidation can be made to approach the running maximum on the year, so with optimal intra-year liquidation
$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}X_{t}] > E[X_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}$.
The gain is the volatility/timing option value created by the $20\%$ weekly moves and the free 31st-year window.

The dominance is in expectation only. On a realised history $V_{B}^{*}$ can finish below $V_{A}$ because of the $20\%$ weekly moves, so $E$ and $H$ are false and no pathwise necessity holds. $A$ is the reverse mean ordering. Under the martingale-M reading the stochastic integral $\int h_{t}dM_{t}$ has zero mean and the best-in-mean causal rule is to hold to $T$, giving $E[V_{B}^{*}]=E[X_{31}]=V_{A}$ – the economic content usually coded as $C$. That reading requires $M$ to be a martingale, i.e. constant autocovariance of returns, which is inconsistent with the stated constant autocovariance of levels and the “random walk around a mean” description.

Current best reading of the problem statement is trend-stationary $M$ with constant autocovariance. Under that reading the strongest true comparative statement in the list is the strict mean dominance of the optimally timed volatile basket, $G$. The formal martingale statements $B,C,D,F$ remain false for the price level, $E$ and $H$ remain false pathwise, and $A$ is false in mean. The unresolved modelling point is whether $M$ is intended as a martingale difference with non-stationary level variance or as a stationary mean-reverting deviation with constant level autocovariance; the question wording points to the latter.

Mean-indifference / C camp 10,11,12,13,14,15,18,2,5,8,9:

10.text:
Basket A is degenerate

$$P^{A}_{t}=T(t)\;\;\hbox{a.s.},\qquad V_{A}=T(31)\hbox{ a.s.}$$

and the 31st year timing window is worthless for A.

On the description given for B

$$P^{B}_{t}=T(t)+Y_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[Y_{t}]=0,$$

with constant autocovariance $ {\rm Cov}(Y_{t},Y_{t+s})=\gamma(s)$,
$Y$ is trend stationary.  In particular

$$E[Y_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\rho^{\,s}Y_{t},\qquad |\rho|<1,
\qquad E[Y_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]-Y_{t}<0\; \hbox{on }\{Y_{t}>0\},$$

i.e. a $10\%$ p.a. linear trend plus a stationary mean-reverting deviation.
For a fixed calendar date $E[P^{B}_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}]$ and both level
processes are $10\%$ drift sub-martingales under $P$.  The formal
martingale premises in B,C,D,F are therefore false in price levels; $A$
is not a martingale and $F$ is false, $B$ is not a physical martingale
and $D$ is false.

Let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction still held in the 31st year,
$h_{30}=1$, $h_{31}=0$, $d(-h)$ the sale measure.  With
$X_{t}=T(t)+Y_{t}$,

$$V_{B}(h)=\int_{30}^{31}X_{t}d(-h_{t})
        =\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+\int_{30}^{31}Y_{t}d(-h_{t}).$$

Mean reversion makes the second term signable: for $Y_{t}>0$
$E[Y_{T}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\rho^{T-t}Y_{t}<Y_{t}$ and the sale
$X_{t}-E[X_{T}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=(1-\rho^{T-t})Y_{t}-\mu(T-t)$ is
positive for $Y_{t}$ large enough.  A price contingent rule which sells
more when a new intra-year high is reached and holds when the price is
below trend harvests the positive deviation before reversion erodes it.
In the limit the attainable payoff is the Snell envelope of the drifted
trend-stationary process on $[30,31]$, i.e. the running maximum of the
year,

$$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]
      >E\!\left[P^{B}_{31}\right]=T(31)=V_{A},$$

with strict inequality as soon as $\sigma_{Y}>0$.  The $20\%$ weekly
volatility makes $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}Y_{t}]>0$, the classic
$E[\max X_{t}]>E[X_{T}]$ convexity.  The gain is in mean only: on a
realised path $V_{B}^{*}$ can finish below $V_{A}$, so the pathwise
necessity claims $E$ and $H$ are false and $A$ is the reverse ordering.

Hence under the constant-autocovariance, trend-stationary reading that
the statement invokes the optimally timed volatile basket strictly
dominates the deterministic basket in unconditional mean.  The only
comparative mean statement in the list that survives is

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

the increase being the volatility/timing option value of the free
31st-year liquidation window.  No almost-sure ordering holds. ∎

1.text:
Basket A is degenerate

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\ {\rm a.s.}$ up to the linear/compound reading, so for any admissible
31st-year liquidation

$V_{A}^{*}\equiv P_{0}1.10^{31}\ {\rm a.s.},\qquad E[V_{A}^{*}]=V_{A}^{*}$,

and the timing window is worthless for A. $P^{A}$ is not a martingale and
$F$ is false.

Write B in the 31st year on the common 10 % trend as

$P^{B}_{t}=T(t)+Y_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[Y_{t}]=0,$

with the $Y$–component stationary with constant autocovariance.  The
statement is that $Y$ is a random walk around the mean, i.e. trend
stationary,

$E[Y_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\rho^{\Delta}Y_{t},\qquad0<\rho<1,$

and not a martingale increment.  Hence on the physical measure

$E[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]
 =T(t+\Delta)+\rho^{\Delta}Y_{t}
 =P^{B}_{t}+\mu\Delta+(\rho^{\Delta}-1)Y_{t}$,

so $P^{B}$ is a strict $10\%$ drift sub-martingale under $\mathbb P$, not a
physical martingale.  The martingale prefaces in B,C,D are therefore
formally false in price levels and $D$ is false because B has the $10\%$
physical drift.  For a fixed calendar date

$E[P^{B}_{T}]=T(T)=E[P^{A}_{T}]$,

so the two baskets are first-moment identical on a fixed horizon.

The 31st year is an American look window.  Let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the
adapted fraction still held, $h_{30}=1,\;h_{31}=0$, and
$V^{B}_{h}=\int_{30}^{31}P^{B}_{t}d(-h_{t})$.  Then

$E[V^{B}_{h}]
 =E\!\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+E\!\int_{30}^{31}Y_{t}d(-h_{t})$.

The trend term is bounded above by $\mu 31$ with equality only for the
terminal sale.  Because $E[Y_{t+\Delta}\mid Y_{t}]=\rho^{\Delta}Y_{t}<Y_{t}$
on $\{Y_{t}>0\}$, the $Y$-integral can be made strictly positive in
expectation by a price contingent rule which sells more when $Y_{t}>0$
and sells less when $Y_{t}<0$, i.e. by harvesting a positive deviation
before mean reversion erodes it.  In the limit the attainable payoff is
the Snell envelope of the trend-stationary process on $[30,31]$,

$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]
      >E[P^{B}_{31}]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}^{*}$,

the strict inequality being $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}Y_{t}]>0$ for
$\sigma_{Y}>0$.  The $20\%$ weekly moves make $\sigma_{Y}>0$ so the
American-type timing option in the free liquidation year is strictly
valuable in expectation.  The gain is the classic volatility /
timing option value $E[\max X_{t}]>E[X_{T}]$.

The dominance is in mean only.  On a realised history $P^{B}$ can and
does finish below $P^{A}$ because of the $\pm20\%$ weekly moves, so the
pathwise necessity claims $E$ and $H$ are false and $A$ is the reverse
ordering.  The price processes are $10\%$ drift sub-martingales, so the
formal martingale statements B,C,D,F are false in the strict price
sense and $F$ is false because $A$ is degenerate.

Hence the only comparative mean statement that survives under the
intended trend-stationary, constant-autocovariance reading is the strict
expected-value dominance of the optimally timed volatile basket over the
deterministic basket,

$E[V_{B}^{*}]>E[V_{A}^{*}]$,

i.e. $G$.  No almost-sure ordering holds.  Under the martingale-increment
interpretation $E\int M_{t}dq_{t}=0$ and the mean indifference content
usually coded as $C$ is obtained for a fixed calendar liquidation, but
that interpretation contradicts the stated constant autocovariance /
random walk around a mean specification. ∎

7.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the physical measure

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\;\;{\rm a.s.}$,

so that with any admissible liquidation in the 31st year

$V_{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\ {\rm a.s.},\qquad E[V_{A}]=V_{A}$,

and the 31st year timing window is inert for A.  $P^{A}$ is not a
martingale under $P$, it is a strict $10\%$ p.a. sub-martingale, and F is
false.

Put the B level on the same trend scale

$P^{B}_{t}=T(t)+Y_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[Y_{t}]=0,$

with $Y$ trend stationary, ${\rm Cov}\!\left(Y_{t},Y_{s}\right)=\gamma(t-s)$
constant in $t-s$, and in particular
$E[Y_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]=\rho^{\,t-s}Y_{s}$, $0<\rho<1$, i.e. a
stationary zero-mean deviation about the $10\%$ p.a. linear trend.
For a fixed calendar date

$E[P^{B}_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}],\qquad 
E[P^{B}_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]=P^{B}_{s}+\mu(t-s)+(\rho^{t-s}-1)Y_{s},$

so both price levels are strict $P$-sub-martingales with the same
$10\%$ physical drift.  In return space the innovations are stationary
zero mean, so the drift-adjusted returns are stationary, but the price
levels are not physical martingales.  The formal martingale prefaces in
B,C,D are therefore inexact for the levels and D is false.

The 31st year is an American look window.  With $\sigma_{B}>0$

$M_{31}:=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\ {\rm a.s.}$

and $E[M_{31}\mid{\cal F}_{30}]>E[P^{B}_{31}\mid{\cal F}_{30}]$.
The Snell envelope of a drifted trend-stationary process is strictly
above the European payoff.  Let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction
still held in $[30,31]$, $h_{30}=1$, $h_{31}=0$, $d(-h)\ge0$.  Then

$V^{B}_{h}=\int_{30}^{31}P^{B}_{t}d(-h_{t})
        =\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+\int_{30}^{31}Y_{t}d(-h_{t})$

and because $E[Y_{t+\Delta}\mid Y_{t}]=\rho^{\Delta}Y_{t}<Y_{t}$ for
$Y_{t}>0$,

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}Y_{t}d(-h_{t})\right]>0$

for any non-trivial price-contingent rule which puts sale weight on
$Y_{t}>0$ and holds on $Y_{t}<0$.  In the limit the attainable payoff
can be made to track the running maximum of the year, i.e.

$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]
      >E[P^{B}_{31}]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A},$

the strict inequality being $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}Y_{t}]>0$ for
$\sigma_{Y}>0$.  This is the classic $E[\max X_{t}]>E[X_{T}]$ volatility
/ timing option value of the free 31st-year liquidation window.

The dominance is in mean only.  On a realised history
$P^{B}$ can and does finish below $P^{A}$ because of the $\pm20\%$
weekly moves, so the pathwise necessity claims $E$ and $H$ are false
and $A$ is the reverse ordering.  The price processes are $10\%$ drift
sub-martingales under $P$, not physical martingales, so B,C,D,F are
false in the literal martingale form.

Hence in expectation the optimally timed volatile basket dominates the
deterministic basket, with no almost-sure dominance.  That is

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

the strictly positive gap being the intra-year American timing option
value.  The mean equality often quoted as C is the fixed-date
European first moment $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$; it is not the
expectation of the optimally adapted liquidation in the 31st year. ∎

6.text:
Basket A is degenerate in levels. On the compound reading

$P_{t}^{A}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\;\;a.s.$

and for every admissible liquidation $q_{t}$ on the 31st year

$V_{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\;\;a.s.,\qquad E[V_{A}]=V_{A}.$

Write B in the 31st year as the deterministic trend plus a stationary
deviation

$P_{t}^{B}=T(t)+M_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[M_{t}]=0,$

with $M_{t}$ a stationary zero-mean process with constant autocovariance
and $E[M_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\rho^{\Delta}M_{t}$, $0<\rho<1$, i.e.
the ‘random walk around a moving mean’ described in the text.  For a
fixed calendar date

$E[P_{t}^{B}]=T(t)=E[P_{t}^{A}]$

so the two baskets have the same $10\%$ p.a. physical drift in first
moment.  The price levels are $10\%$ drifted sub–martingales under $P$,
not physical martingales.  In particular $P^{A}$ is deterministic so $F$
is false and the literal martingale prefaces in B,C,D are false in the
price level; D is false because $B$ has the $10\%$ drift.

Let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction still held on
$[30,31]$, $h_{30}=1,\;h_{31}=0$.  With $d(-h)$ the sale measure

$V_{B}(h)=\int_{30}^{31}P_{t}^{B}d(-h_{t})
        =\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}d(-h_{t}) .$

With mean reversion

$E\!\left[P_{t+\Delta}^{B}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\right]
   =P_{t}^{B}+\mu\Delta+(\rho^{\Delta}-1)M_{t}<P_{t}^{B}+\mu\Delta$
on $\{M_{t}>0\}$ and $>P_{t}^{B}+\mu\Delta$ on $\{M_{t}<0\}$.
Hence a price contingent rule which sells more when $M_{t}>0$ and holds
when $M_{t}<0$ can make

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}d(-h_{t})\right]>0$

because the positive deviation is harvested before the mean-reverting
erosion $\rho^{\Delta}-1<0$ sets in.  The 31st year is an
American look window.  With $\sigma_{B}>0$

$M_{31}:=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_{t}^{B}\ge P_{31}^{B}\;a.s.$
and 
$E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_{t}^{B}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\right]
   >E\!\left[P_{31}^{B}\mid{\cal F}_{30}\right]$.

The Snell envelope of the drifted trend-stationary price is strictly
above the European payoff and with a price-contingent liquidation that
loads sale weight on intra-year highs the attainable mean can be made to
track the running maximum. In the limit

$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_{t}^{B}\right]
      >E[P_{31}^{B}]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}.$

The gain is the classic volatility/timing option value of the free
31st-year liquidation window and it is strictly positive because the
weekly $\pm20\%$ moves make $\sigma_{B}>0$.  It is a mean gain only: on a
realised history $V_{B}^{*}$ can and does finish below $V_{A}$,
so the pathwise necessity claims $E$ and $H$ are false, $A$ is the
reverse mean ordering and the deterministic basket $A$ can never dominate
$B$ pathwise.

Hence the only comparative statement in the list that survives under the
intended trend-stationary, intra-year optimally timed liquidation is the
strict mean dominance of the volatile basket,

$E[V_{B}^{*}]>E[V_{A}]$,

i.e. G.  The dominance is in expectation only, no almost-sure ordering
holds, and the formal martingale statements B,C,D,F are false on the
strict price level.  That is the strongest true comparative claim in the
set. ∎

12.text:
Basket A is degenerate in levels

$V_{A}\equiv P_{0}1.10^{31}\;\;{\rm a.s.}$

and the whole 31st year window is worthless for A.  Write the B
level on the 10 % trend as

$P_{t}^{B}=T(t)+M_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[M_{t}]=0,$

with $M_{t}$ stationary, ${\rm Cov}(M_{t},M_{s})$ a function of $t-s$, i.e.
trend stationary.  For a fixed calendar date

$E[P_{t}^{B}]=T(t)=E[P_{t}^{A}]$,

so the two baskets have the same $10\%$ p.a. physical drift and the
price levels are strict $P$-sub-martingales.  The “martingale’’ prefaces
in B,C,D,F are therefore false in price levels; $P^{A}$ is degenerate
so F is false and $P^{B}$ has the $10\%$ drift so D is false.

On $[30,31]$ the trader can choose an adapted liquidation
$h_{t}\in[0,1]$, $h_{30}=1$, $h_{31}=0$.  With
$C_{h}=\int_{30}^{31}P_{t}^{B}d(-h_{t})$

$C_{h}= \int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}d(-h_{t}) $.

$M_{t}$ is mean reverting, $E[M_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]
 =\rho^{s}M_{t}$ with $|\rho|<1$, so a price contingent rule can put
sale weight on $M_{t}>0$ and less weight on $M_{t}<0$.  In particular
$E[M_{\tau}]>0$ for a stopping time $\tau$ which is increasing in
$M_{t}$, and

$E[P_{\tau}^{B}]=\mu E[\tau]+E[M_{\tau}]
      >\mu E[\tau]$.

The loss of drift from stopping a little early,
$\mu\,(31-E[\tau])$, can be made arbitrarily small while $E[M_{\tau}]$
remains bounded away from zero because $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}M_{t}]>0$
for $\sigma_{B}>0$.  In the limit the admissible payoff converges to the
Snell envelope of the trend stationary price on the year,

$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_{t}^{B}\right]
      >E[P_{31}^{B}]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}$,

the strict inequality being the classic
$E[\max_{t}X_{t}]> \max_{t}E[X_{t}]$ convexity of a non-degenerate
drifted stationary process.  The gain is the American / intra-year
timing option value created by the $\pm20\%$ weekly moves.

The dominance is in mean only.  On a realised history $P^{B}$ can
finish well below $P^{A}$, so the pathwise necessity claims

$E\;:$ $V_{A}\ge V_{B}\ {\rm a.s.}$ , $H\;:$ $V_{B}\ge V_{A}\ {\rm a.s.}$

are false and the reverse mean claim A is false.  The expected
liquidation value of the optimally liquidated volatile basket is
strictly larger than the deterministic liquidation value of A, i.e.

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

with no almost sure ordering.  The formal martingale statements B–D–F
are false on the physical $10\%$ drift; the economic content is the
mean option value of the free 31st-year liquidation window.

17.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the physical measure

$V^{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\ {\rm a.s.}$ and the 31st year window is inert for A.
For a fixed calendar date

$E[P^{B}_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}],\qquad E[P^{B}_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]
      =P^{B}_{s}+\mu(t-s)$,

so both level processes are strict $10\%$ p.a. sub-martingales under $P$.
The price levels are not physical martingales and the stationary-return
$\to$ martingale prefaces in B,C,D,F are formally false in the level.
In particular $P^{A}$ is deterministic so F is false and $B$ has the
$10\%$ physical drift so D is false.

Write the B level in the 31st year as trend stationary

$P^{B}_{t}=T(t)+Y_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[Y_{t}]=0,$
$E[Y_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\rho^{\,s}Y_{t},\;0<\rho<1,$

i.e. $10\%$ p.a. drift in mean and stationary zero mean noise with
constant autocovariance, the “random walk around a mean with drift’’
described in the statement.  On a fixed horizon $E[P^{B}_{T}]=T(T)=
E[P^{A}_{T}]$.

The 31st year is an American look window.  With $\sigma_{B}>0$

$M_{31}:=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\ {\rm a.s.}$,
$E[M_{31}\mid{\cal F}_{30}]>E[P^{B}_{31}\mid{\cal F}_{30}]$,
and the Snell envelope of the drifted trend-stationary process is
strictly above the European payoff.  An adapted increasing liquidation
$h_{t}\in[0,1]$ can put more weight on intra-year highs and less weight
on intra-year lows and harvest the mean-reverting deviation $Y_{t}$
before it is eroded,

$E[V^{B}_{h}] =E\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+E\int_{30}^{31}Y_{t}d(-h_{t})$,

and $E\int Y_{t}d(-h_{t})>0$ can be made strictly positive by a
price-contingent rule which sells more when a new intra-year high is
reached and holds when the price is below trend.  In the limit

$E[V^{*}_{B}]\ge E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]
      >E[P^{B}_{31}]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V^{A}$,

the strict inequality being $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}Y_{t}]>0$ for
$\sigma_{Y}>0$.  This is the classic volatility / timing option value
$E[\max X_{t}]>E[X_{T}]$.

The dominance is in mean only.  On a realised history $P^{B}$ can and
does finish below $P^{A}$ because of the $\pm20\%$ weekly moves, so the
pathwise necessity claims E and H are false and $A$ is the reverse
ordering.  The price processes are $10\%$ drift sub-martingales, not
physical martingales, so B,C,D,F are false in the literal martingale
form.  The only comparative mean statement that survives in the list
under the trend-stationary / state-contingent liquidation reading is
the strict mean dominance of the optimally timed volatile basket,

$E[V^{*}_{B}]>E[V_{A}]$,

i.e. G, with no almost-sure ordering.  The economically relevant
first-moment indifference $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ for a fixed
calendar liquidation is the content usually coded as C, but it is not
attainable once a causal intra-year liquidation is allowed for a
trend-stationary deviation. ∎

18.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the physical measure

$V_{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\equiv V_{0}$ a.s.

and the 31st year look window is worthless for A.  Write B in the
31st year on the $10\%$ trend scale as

$P_{t}^{B}=T(t)+Y_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[Y_{t}]=0,$

with $Y_{t}$ trend stationary, $E[Y_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]
=\rho^{s}Y_{t}$, $0<\rho<1$, constant autocovariance, $ {\rm Var}[Y_{t}]$
$>0$.  In particular for a fixed calendar date

$E[P_{t}^{B}]=T(t)=E[P_{t}^{A}],\qquad 
E[P_{t}^{B}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]=P_{s}^{B}+\mu(t-s)+(\rho^{\,t-s}-1)Y_{s},$

so the price levels are $10\%$ drifted strict sub-martingales under $P$,
not physical martingales.  The “martingale’’ prefaces in B,C,D,F are
therefore false in the price level and $F$ is false because $A$ is
deterministic.

On $[30,31]$ let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction still held,
$h_{30}=1$, $h_{31}=0$,

$V^{B}_{h}= \int_{30}^{31}P^{B}_{t}d(-h_{t})
        =\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+\int_{30}^{31}Y_{t}d(-h_{t}) .
$

Because $E[Y_{t+s}\mid Y_{t}]=\rho^{s}Y_{t}<Y_{t}$ for $Y_{t}>0$,
$E[Y_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]-Y_{s}=( \rho^{t-s}-1)Y_{s}$ has the sign of
$-Y_{s}$.  Hence

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}Y_{t}d(-h_{t})\right]>0$

for any non-trivial price contingent rule which puts more sale weight
on $Y_{t}>0$ and less on $Y_{t}<0$.  The rule can be made to sell more
when a new intra-year high is reached and to hold when the price is
below trend, i.e. to harvest the mean-reverting deviation before it is
eroded.  In the limit the attainable payoff is the Snell envelope of the
trend stationary process on $[30,31]$

$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]
      >E[P^{B}_{31}]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A},$

strictly because $\sigma_{Y}>0$ and $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}Y_{t}]>0$.
The gain is the classic volatility / timing option value
$E[\max X_{t}]>E[X_{T}]$ created by the free 31st-year liquidation
window.

The dominance is mean only. On a realised history $P^{B}$ can and does
finish below $P^{A}$ because of the $\pm20\%$ weekly moves, so the
pathwise necessity claims $E$ and $H$ are false and $A$ is the reverse
ordering.  The price processes are $10\%$ drift sub-martingales under
$P$, so B,C,D,F are false in the literal martingale form.  The only
comparative mean statement which survives in the list under the
trend-stationary, mean-reverting reading of “random walk around a mean
with drift’’ is the strict mean dominance of the optimally timed
volatile basket,

$E[V_{B}^{*}]>E[V_{A}]$,

i.e. G.  The increase is in expectation only, no almost-sure ordering
holds.  On the strict random-walk-with-drift, i.e. $M$ a martingale,
reading $E[\int M_{t}dq_{t}]=0$ and the best-in-mean causal liquidation
is $q_{t}\equiv0$ on $[30,31)$, $E[V_{B}^{*}]=E[P^{B}_{31}]=V_{A}$,
the usual first-moment indifference usually coded as C. ∎

16.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the physical measure

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}\quad{\rm a.s.}$

so that with any admissible 31st year liquidation

$V^{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}$ a.s. and $E[V^{A}]=V^{A}$.

Write B on the common trend scale as

$P^{B}_{t}=T(t)+Y_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad 
E[Y_{t}]=0,$

with $Y_{t}$ stationary, ${\rm Cov}\big(Y_{t},Y_{s}\big)=\gamma(t-s)$
constant in the sense of stationarity and $Y$ trend stationary.
Hence on a fixed calendar date

$E[P^{B}_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}]$,

$E[r^{B}_{t}]=E[r^{A}_{t}]=10\%$ p.a. in first moment.
In levels $E[P^{B}_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]
 =T(t+s)+\rho^{s}Y_{t}$ with $|\rho|<1$, i.e.

$E\!\left[P^{B}_{t+ds}\mid{\cal F}_{t}\right]-P^{B}_{t}
 =\mu ds+(\rho^{ds}-1)Y_{t}$.

The price level is not a $P$-martingale and $P^{A}$ is not a
martingale. The formal martingale prefaces in B,C,D,F are therefore
formally false on the price level; in particular F is false because A
is degenerate and D is false because B has a $10\%$ physical drift.

Let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction still held on $[30,31]$,
$h_{30}=1$, $h_{31}=0$ and $d(-h)$ the sale measure.  Cash is

$V^{B}_{h}= \int_{30}^{31}P^{B}_{t}d(-h_{t})
        =\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+\int_{30}^{31}Y_{t}d(-h_{t})  $.

The second term is in general non-zero.  For a predictable $h$

$E\!\left[Y_{t}d(-h_{t})\right]
   =E\!\left[E[Y_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{t-}]\,d(-h_{t})\right]
   =E\!\left[\rho^{\Delta}Y_{t-}\,d(-h_{t})\right]$,

so a price contingent rule which sells more when $Y_{t}>0$ and sells
less when $Y_{t}<0$ makes $E\int Y_{t}d(-h_{t})>0$.  Mean reversion
makes $E[P^{B}_{t+ds}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]-P^{B}_{t}<\mu ds$ on
$\{Y_{t}>0\}$ and $>\mu ds$ on $\{Y_{t}<0\}$; selling the positive
deviation before it is eroded and holding the negative deviation
longer raises the unconditional mean.

In the limit the attainable payoff is the Snell envelope of the
trend stationary process on $[30,31]$,

$E[V^{B*}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]
      >E\!\left[P^{B}_{31}\right]=T(31)$,

with strict inequality as soon as $\sigma_{Y}>0$.  With the $20\%$
weekly moves $\sigma_{Y}>0$ and

$E[V^{B*}]>T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V^{A}$.

The dominance is in mean only. On a realised history $P^{B}$ can and
does finish below $P^{A}$ because of the $\pm20\%$ weekly moves, so
the pathwise necessity claims E and H are false and the reverse mean
claim A is false.  The 31st year timing option is a classic
volatility/timing option value; volatility raises dispersion and the
ex-post supremum $E[\sup P^{B}_{t}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]$, it does not give an
almost sure ordering.

The only comparative mean statement in the list that survives is
the strict mean dominance of the optimally timed volatile basket over
the deterministic basket,

$E[V_{B}^{*}]>E[V_{A}]$,

i.e. G.  The price processes are $10\%$ drifted sub-martingales in the
unconditional sense, not physical martingales, so B,C,D,F are false in
the literal martingale form and E,H are false pathwise. ∎

4.text:
Under $P$ the two baskets have the same physical first moment

$E[P_{t}^{A}] =E[P_{t}^{B}]=T(t),\qquad T'(t)/T(t)=10\%\;{\rm p.a.}$

and $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s.  so that with any admissible liquidation
in the 31st year

$V_{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}\;\;\hbox{a.s.}$ , $E[V_{A}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}$ .

Write the $B$ level in the $31st$ year as

$X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[M_{t}]=0$

with $M$ stationary, $ {\rm Cov}\!\left(M_{t},M_{t+s}\right)=\gamma(s)$,
$0<\rho<1$, $E[M_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\rho^{s}M_{t}$.
Hence in price levels

$E[X_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=X_{t}+\mu s+(\rho^{s}-1)M_{t}
<X_{t}+\mu s$ on $\{M_{t}>0\}$

so $X$ is a strict $10\%$ drift sub-martingale, not a
physical martingale, and the martingale prefaces in B,C,D,F are
formally false; in particular $P^{A}$ is degenerate.

Let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction still held on $[30,31]$,
$h_{30}=1$, $h_{31}=0$, $d(-h)$ the admissible liquidation measure.
With integration by parts

$V_{B}(h)=\int_{30}^{31}X_{t}d(-h_{t})
        =X_{31}-\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}\,dX_{t}$,

$E[V_{B}(h)]=T(31)-\mu E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}dt-E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}dM_{t}$.

For the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck / trend-stationary realisation
$dM_{t}= -\lambda M_{t}dt+\sigma dW_{t}$, $\lambda>0$,

$E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}dM_{t}= -\lambda E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}M_{t}dt$,
and

$E[V_{B}(h)]= \mu\Bigl(1-E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}dt\Bigr)
       +\lambda E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}M_{t}dt  $

on the normalised interval.  The second term can be made strictly
positive by a price contingent rule which sells more when a new
intra-year high $M_{t}>0$ is reached and holds when $M_{t}<0$, i.e.
by harvesting the mean-reverting deviation before it is eroded.
In the limit the attainable payoff is the Snell envelope of the
drifted stationary price on $[30,31]$,

$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le 31}X_{t}\right]
      >E\!\left[X_{31}\right]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}$,

the strict inequality being $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}M_{t}]>0$ for
$\sigma_{M}>0$.  The gain is the classic volatility/timing option
value of the free 31st-year look window,
$E[\max X_{t}]>E[X_{T}]$.  It is a mean gain only: on a realised
history $V_{B}^{*}$ can and does finish below $V_{A}$, so $E$ and $H$
are false pathwise and $A$ is the reverse ordering.  The price
processes are $10\%$ drift sub-martingales under $P$, so $B,C,D,F$
are false in the literal martingale sense.  The economically
relevant first moment ordering under optimal intra-year liquidation is
the strict expected-value dominance of the optimally timed volatile
basket.

Hence on the trend-stationary reading intended by constant
autocovariance the optimally liquidated $B$ basket dominates $A$ in
expectation, i.e. $G$.  No almost-sure ordering holds. ∎

11.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the physical measure and the intra-year window is
worthless for A

$V_{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}$ a.s., $E[V_{A}]=V_{A}$.

Write B in the 31st year in level form after detrending

$X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad 
E[M_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]=M_{s},\;E[M_{t}]=0 $

up to the usual linear/compound reading.  On a fixed calendar date

$E[X_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}],\qquad
E[X_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]=X_{s}+\mu(t-s)$,

i.e. the two baskets have the same $10\%$ p.a. physical drift in first
moment.  In price levels the processes are strict $10\%$ drifted
sub-martingales under ${\mathbb P}$, not physical martingales.  The
‘return distribution is stationary $\to$ martingale’ prefaces in
B,C,D,F are therefore formally inaccurate for the price level; in
particular $A$ is degenerate so F is false and B is not a physical
martingale so D is false.

Let $q_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction already sold on $[30,31]$,
$q_{30}=0$, $q_{31}=1$, $dq_{t}\ge0$ predictable and
$C_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}X_{t}dq_{t}$.
With $X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t}$

$C_{q}= \int T(t)dq_{t}+\int M_{t}dq_{t}$,
$\displaystyle\int M_{t}dq_{t}=M_{31}q_{31}-M_{30}q_{30}-\int q_{t}dM_{t}$,

so that for every predictable $q$

$E\!\left[\int M_{t}dq_{t}\right]=0$ .

Hence

$E[C_{q}]=\mu\,E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}t\,dq_{t}\right]
       =\mu\Bigl[31-E\!\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt\Bigr]\le\mu\,31$,

with equality iff $q_{t}\equiv0$ on $[30,31)$ and the whole position is
sold at the terminal instant $T=31$.  For a stopping time $\tau\le31$

$E[X_{\tau}]=\mu E[\tau]+E[M_{\tau}]\le\mu31=E[X_{31}]$,

so the mean maximising admissible, i.e. causal predictable, liquidation
is to hold to the very end of the admissible window.  In particular

$E[V_{B}^{*}]=E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}$

in first moment.  The 20% weekly moves change the second moment only.
Indeed

$E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]>E\!\left[P^{B}_{31}\right]$

is true for the ex-post random variable $\sup_{t}P^{B}_{t}$, but
$\sup_{t}P^{B}_{t}$ is not an attainable adapted payoff: the time of the
overall intra-year maximum is not a stopping time and

$E\!\left[\int M_{t}d(-q_{t})\right]=0$

for every predictable sale plan.  The classic
$E[\max X_{t}]>\max E[X_{t}]$ convexity is a dispersion / ex-post
statement, not an unconditional mean premium to an adapted liquidation.

Hence in unconditional mean the two strategies are indistinguishable:
the same $10\%$ p.a. drift drives the mean and the stationary zero-mean
weekly $\pm20\%$ innovations raise risk, not expected return.
Pathwise dominance $E,H$ is false and the mean dominance $A,G$ is false
under admissible causal liquidation.  The economic content that survives
in the list is the first-moment indifference, the usual loose
‘drift-adjusted returns are zero mean and stationary’ statement
labelled C, with the formal martingale wording being loose on the
price level.  In particular $E$ and $H$ are false pathwise and the
strict mean dominance claimed in $G$ is the unattainable ex-post
$E[\sup]$ fallacy.

3.text:
Constant autocovariance of the level deviations is the key.  Write the
31st year on the same scale

$X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[M_{t}]=0,$

with $M$ stationary, ${\rm Cov}(M_{t},M_{s})$ depending only on
$|t-s|$ and $\sigma_{M}>0$.  After detrending $E[M_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal
F}_{t}]=\rho^{\Delta}M_{t}$ with $|\rho|<1$; the process is
trend-stationary, not a martingale difference. On a fixed calendar date

$E[X_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}],\qquad E[r^{B}_{t}]=E[r^{A}_{t}]=10\%$ p.a.,

so the two baskets have the same unconditional first moment and
$P^{A}$ is degenerate $P^{A}_{31}=P_{0}1.10^{31}$ a.s.  In price levels
both are $10\%$ drift sub-martingales in the mean, they are not physical
martingales and the martingale prefaces in B,C,D,F are formally false.
$P^{A}$ is deterministic so $F$ is false.

Let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction still held in the 31st
year, $h_{30}=1$, $h_{31}=0$, $d(-h)\ge0$ the sale measure.  Then

$V_{h}= \int_{30}^{31}X_{t}d(-h_{t})
     =\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}d(-h_{t}) .$

$E[\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})]\le T(31)$ with equality only for the
terminal sale, and

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}d(-h_{t})\right]
   =k\,E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}^{2}dt\right]+o(k)>0$

for any price-contingent rule which sells more when $M_{t}>0$ and less
when $M_{t}<0$.  With

$E[X_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]
   =X_{t}+\mu\Delta+(\rho^{\Delta}-1)M_{t},$

a positive deviation $M_{t}>0$ has a negative conditional drift
$(\rho^{\Delta}-1)M_{t}<0$, i.e. the transitory component is expected to
mean-revert.  Selling into the positive deviation therefore harvests
the transitory premium before it is eroded, the loss of a little drift
accrual $\mu\Delta$ being more than compensated by the
$E[M_{t}^{2}]$ term when $\sigma_{M}$ is the $20\%$ weekly moves quoted
in the statement. In the limit the attainable mean is the Snell envelope
of the trend-stationary process on $[30,31]$,

$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}X_{t}\right]
      >E[X_{31}]=T(31)$,

and in particular

$E[V_{B}^{*}]>E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V^{A}\quad a.s.$

The dominance is in mean only.  On a realised history $X_{t}$ can and
does finish below $P^{A}_{31}$ because of the $ \pm20\%$ weekly moves,
so the pathwise necessity statements $E$ and $H$ are false and the
reverse mean ordering $A$ is false.  The strictly positive gap is the
classic volatility/timing option value of the free 31st-year liquidation
window for a trend-stationary, mean-reverting deviation.  That is the
strict mean dominance of the optimally liquidated volatile basket over
the deterministic basket,

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A,

with no almost-sure ordering.  The formal martingale statements
B,C,D,F are false on the physical $10\%$ drift; the first-moment
indifference they are intended to capture holds only for a fixed
calendar liquidation date and for a martingale-detrended $M$, which is
not the constant-autocovariance trend-stationary specification here.

Then for a fixed calendar date $E[X_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}]$ and
$E[X_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=X_{s}+\mu(t-s)$. The two baskets have the same 10% p.a. physical drift in first moment and the price levels are strict $P$-sub-martingales, not physical martingales. The “martingale” language is shorthand for drift-adjusted returns being stationary zero-mean.

Let $q_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction already sold, $dq_{t}\ge0$ predictable, $q_{30}=0$, $q_{31}=1$. Cash raised on $[30,31]$ is

$C_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}X_{t}dq_{t}
     =\int_{30}^{31}T(t)dq_{t}+\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}dq_{t}.$

For every predictable $q$, $E[\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}dq_{t}]=0$ by integration by parts
$\int M\,dq = M_{31}q_{31}-M_{30}q_{30}-\int q\,dM$ and $E\int q\,dM=0$. Hence

$E[C_{q}]=\mu\,E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}t\,dq_{t}\right]
       =\mu\Bigl[31-E\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt\Bigr]\le \mu31,$

with equality iff $q_{t}\equiv0$ on $[30,31)$ and the whole position is sold at the terminal instant. For a stopping time $\tau\le31$,

$E[X_{\tau}]=\mu E[\tau]+E[M_{\tau}]\le\mu31=E[X_{31}]$,

so the mean-maximising admissible liquidation is to hold to the very end of the window. Selling more when $M_{t}>0$ shortens the average holding of the positive drift and $E\int M_{t}dq_{t}=0$, so the martingale component contributes nothing to the unconditional mean.

so both level processes are strict $10\%$ p.a. sub-martingales under $P$.
The price levels are not physical martingales and the stationary-return
$\to$ martingale prefaces in B,C,D,F are formally false in the level.
In particular $P^{A}$ is deterministic so F is false and $B$ has the
$10\%$ physical drift so D is false.

Write the B level in the 31st year as trend stationary

$P^{B}_{t}=T(t)+Y_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[Y_{t}]=0,$
$E[Y_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\rho^{\,s}Y_{t},\;0<\rho<1,$

i.e. $10\%$ p.a. drift in mean and stationary zero mean noise with
constant autocovariance, the “random walk around a mean with drift’’
described in the statement.  On a fixed horizon $E[P^{B}_{T}]=T(T)=
E[P^{A}_{T}]$.

The 31st year is an American look window.  With $\sigma_{B}>0$

$M_{31}:=\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\ge P^{B}_{31}\ {\rm a.s.}$,
$E[M_{31}\mid{\cal F}_{30}]>E[P^{B}_{31}\mid{\cal F}_{30}]$,
and the Snell envelope of the drifted trend-stationary process is
strictly above the European payoff.  An adapted increasing liquidation
$h_{t}\in[0,1]$ can put more weight on intra-year highs and less weight
on intra-year lows and harvest the mean-reverting deviation $Y_{t}$
before it is eroded,

$E[V^{B}_{h}] =E\int_{30}^{31}T(t)d(-h_{t})+E\int_{30}^{31}Y_{t}d(-h_{t})$,

and $E\int Y_{t}d(-h_{t})>0$ can be made strictly positive by a
price-contingent rule which sells more when a new intra-year high is
reached and holds when the price is below trend.  In the limit

$E[V^{*}_{B}]\ge E\Big[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\Big]
      >E[P^{B}_{31}]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V^{A}$,

the strict inequality being $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}Y_{t}]>0$ for
$\sigma_{Y}>0$.  This is the classic volatility / timing option value
$E[\max X_{t}]>E[X_{T}]$.

does finish below $P^{A}$ because of the $\pm20\%$ weekly moves, so the
pathwise necessity claims E and H are false and $A$ is the reverse
ordering.  The price processes are $10\%$ drift sub-martingales, not
physical martingales, so B,C,D,F are false in the literal martingale
form.  The only comparative mean statement that survives in the list
under the trend-stationary / state-contingent liquidation reading is
the strict mean dominance of the optimally timed volatile basket,

$E[V^{*}_{B}]>E[V_{A}]$,

i.e. G, with no almost-sure ordering.  The economically relevant
first-moment indifference $E[P^{B}_{31}]=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ for a fixed
calendar liquidation is the content usually coded as C, but it is not
attainable once a causal intra-year liquidation is allowed for a
trend-stationary deviation. ∎

Under $P$ the two baskets have the same physical first moment

$E[P_{t}^{A}] =E[P_{t}^{B}]=T(t),\qquad T'(t)/T(t)=10\%\;{\rm p.a.}$

and $P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s.  so that with any admissible liquidation

Write the $B$ level in the $31st$ year as

$X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[M_{t}]=0$

with $M$ stationary, $ {\rm Cov}\!\left(M_{t},M_{t+s}\right)=\gamma(s)$,
$0<\rho<1$, $E[M_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\rho^{s}M_{t}$.
Hence in price levels

$E[X_{t+s}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=X_{t}+\mu s+(\rho^{s}-1)M_{t}
<X_{t}+\mu s$ on $\{M_{t}>0\}$

so $X$ is a strict $10\%$ drift sub-martingale, not a
physical martingale, and the martingale prefaces in B,C,D,F are
formally false; in particular $P^{A}$ is degenerate.

Let $h_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction still held on $[30,31]$,

$V_{B}(h)=\int_{30}^{31}X_{t}d(-h_{t})
        =X_{31}-\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}\,dX_{t}$,

$E[V_{B}(h)]=T(31)-\mu E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}dt-E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}dM_{t}$.

For the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck / trend-stationary realisation
$dM_{t}= -\lambda M_{t}dt+\sigma dW_{t}$, $\lambda>0$,

$E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}dM_{t}= -\lambda E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}M_{t}dt$,
and

$E[V_{B}(h)]= \mu\Bigl(1-E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}dt\Bigr)
       +\lambda E\int_{30}^{31}h_{t}M_{t}dt  $

on the normalised interval.  The second term can be made strictly
positive by a price contingent rule which sells more when a new
intra-year high $M_{t}>0$ is reached and holds when $M_{t}<0$, i.e.
by harvesting the mean-reverting deviation before it is eroded.
In the limit the attainable payoff is the Snell envelope of the
drifted stationary price on $[30,31]$,

$E[V_{B}^{*}]\ge E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le 31}X_{t}\right]
      >E\!\left[X_{31}\right]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}$,

value of the free 31st-year look window,
$E[\max X_{t}]>E[X_{T}]$.  It is a mean gain only: on a realised

processes are $10\%$ drift sub-martingales under $P$, so $B,C,D,F$

relevant first moment ordering under optimal intra-year liquidation is

basket.

Hence on the trend-stationary reading intended by constant
autocovariance the optimally liquidated $B$ basket dominates $A$ in

Basket A is degenerate on the physical measure and the intra-year window is

$V_{A}=P_{0}1.10^{31}$ a.s., $E[V_{A}]=V_{A}$.

Write B in the 31st year in level form after detrending

$X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad 
E[M_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]=M_{s},\;E[M_{t}]=0 $

up to the usual linear/compound reading.  On a fixed calendar date

$E[X_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}],\qquad
E[X_{t}\mid{\cal F}_{s}]=X_{s}+\mu(t-s)$,

i.e. the two baskets have the same $10\%$ p.a. physical drift in first
moment.  In price levels the processes are strict $10\%$ drifted
sub-martingales under ${\mathbb P}$, not physical martingales.  The
‘return distribution is stationary $\to$ martingale’ prefaces in
B,C,D,F are therefore formally inaccurate for the price level; in
particular $A$ is degenerate so F is false and B is not a physical
martingale so D is false.

Let $q_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction already sold on $[30,31]$,
$q_{30}=0$, $q_{31}=1$, $dq_{t}\ge0$ predictable and
$C_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}X_{t}dq_{t}$.
With $X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t}$

$C_{q}= \int T(t)dq_{t}+\int M_{t}dq_{t}$,
$\displaystyle\int M_{t}dq_{t}=M_{31}q_{31}-M_{30}q_{30}-\int q_{t}dM_{t}$,

so that for every predictable $q$

$E\!\left[\int M_{t}dq_{t}\right]=0$ .

Hence

$E[C_{q}]=\mu\,E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}t\,dq_{t}\right]
       =\mu\Bigl[31-E\!\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt\Bigr]\le\mu\,31$,

with equality iff $q_{t}\equiv0$ on $[30,31)$ and the whole position is
sold at the terminal instant $T=31$.  For a stopping time $\tau\le31$

$E[X_{\tau}]=\mu E[\tau]+E[M_{\tau}]\le\mu31=E[X_{31}]$,

so the mean maximising admissible, i.e. causal predictable, liquidation
is to hold to the very end of the admissible window.  In particular

$E[V_{B}^{*}]=E[P^{B}_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}$

in first moment.  The 20% weekly moves change the second moment only.
Indeed

$E\!\left[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P^{B}_{t}\right]>E\!\left[P^{B}_{31}\right]$

is true for the ex-post random variable $\sup_{t}P^{B}_{t}$, but
$\sup_{t}P^{B}_{t}$ is not an attainable adapted payoff: the time of the
overall intra-year maximum is not a stopping time and

$E\!\left[\int M_{t}d(-q_{t})\right]=0$

for every predictable sale plan.  The classic
$E[\max X_{t}]>\max E[X_{t}]$ convexity is a dispersion / ex-post
statement, not an unconditional mean premium to an adapted liquidation.

Hence in unconditional mean the two strategies are indistinguishable:
the same $10\%$ p.a. drift drives the mean and the stationary zero-mean
weekly $\pm20\%$ innovations raise risk, not expected return.

in the list is the first-moment indifference, the usual loose
‘drift-adjusted returns are zero mean and stationary’ statement
labelled C, with the formal martingale wording being loose on the
price level.  In particular $E$ and $H$ are false pathwise and the
strict mean dominance claimed in $G$ is the unattainable ex-post
$E[\sup]$ fallacy.

12.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The core facts are settled: Basket A is degenerate V_A = P0 1.10^{31} a.s., timing in year 31 is worthless. Basket B has same 10% p.a. physical drift in first moment, E[P^B_t]=T(t)=E[P^A_t], price levels are 10% drift sub-martingales, not physical martingales. Return innovations are stationary zero-mean; the formal “return distribution stationary ⇒ martingale’’ prefaces in B,C,D,F are false for price levels, D is false because B has 10% drift, F is false because A is degenerate. E and H are false pathwise.

The split is over attainable mean in the 31st-year liquidation window.

Mean-preserving / predictable-liquidation camp, 11,13,14,2,5,8,9: Write level X_t = T(t)+M_t with M a zero-mean martingale difference, E[M_t|F_s]=M_s. For predictable q_t ∈[0,1] with q_31=1, C_q = ∫T dq + ∫M dq and E[∫M dq]=0 by integration by parts. Hence E[C_q]= μE[∫t dq] ≤ μ31 with equality only for terminal sale. For stopping τ≤31, E[X_τ]= μE[τ]+E[M_τ] ≤ μ31 = E[X_31]. Hence for every admissible causal liquidation E[V_B*]=E[P^B_31]=P0 1.10^31 = V_A. Volatility raises dispersion only, E[sup_{30≤t≤31}X_t] > E[X_31] is true ex-post but sup is not an attainable adapted payoff; the time of the overall intra-year maximum is not a stopping time and no predictable sale plan replicates E[sup] in expectation. The economic content they identify is first-moment indifference, the C statement up to the loose martingale wording.

Option-value / trend-stationary camp, 1,10,12,15,16,17,18,3,4,6: The statement “constant autocovariance”, “random walk around a mean with drift”, implies trend-stationary deviation Y_t with E[Y_{t+s}|F_t]=ρ^s Y_t, 0<ρ<1, not a martingale. Then E[X_{t+Δ}|F_t]=X_t+ μΔ+(ρ^Δ-1)Y_t. A positive deviation is expected to revert, a negative deviation to revert up. A price-contingent rule which sells more when Y_t>0 and holds when Y_t<0, i.e. harvests the deviation before mean reversion erodes it, yields E[∫Y_t d(-h_t)]>0. In the limit the attainable payoff is the Snell envelope of the drifted trend-stationary process on [30,31], and E[V_B*] ≥ E[sup_{30≤t≤31}P^B_t] > E[P^B_31]=T(31)=V_A. With σ_B>0 from 20% weekly moves the American-type intra-year timing option is strictly valuable in expectation. Dominance is in mean only; pathwise dominance fails.

Unresolved is the model reading of B. ARIMA with drift is normally a random walk with drift = martingale difference, which gives mean-preserving C. The wording “constant autocovariance and linear growth trend” and “random walk around a mean with drift” is read by the G camp as trend stationary with mean reversion, giving strict mean dominance G. Both camps agree the martingale prefaces are formally inaccurate and that no almost-sure ordering holds. My current understanding remains bifurcated: under a strict martingale-difference/ predictable-integral interpretation the strongest true comparative statement is the mean indifference content of C; under the trend-stationary/ Snell-envelope interpretation intended by constant autocovariance of levels the strongest true comparative statement is G with E[V_B*] > E[V_A].

The split is about the 31st-year liquidation $q_t$ and the nature of $M_t$ in $P_t^B=T(t)+M_t$.

* Martingale-difference reading: $E[M_{t}\mid\mathcal F_s]=M_s$, $E[\int M_t dq_t]=0$ for predictable $q$. Then
  $E[C_q]=\mu E[\int t dq_t]\le\mu 31$ with equality iff hold to $T=31$.
  For a stopping time $\tau\le31$, $E[X_\tau]=\mu E[\tau]+E[M_\tau]\le\mu31=E[X_{31}]$.
  The predictable integral is mean zero, volatility only raises dispersion.
  $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}X_t]>E[X_{31}]$ is true ex-post but $\sup$ is not an attainable adapted payoff; the time of the overall maximum is not a stopping time.
  Under this reading $E[V_B^*]=E[P_{31}^B]=P_0 1.10^{31}=V_A$, first-moment indifference. * Trend-stationary / constant autocovariance reading: the statement says “constant autocovariance”, “random walk around a mean with drift”, ARIMA with drift but with long-run volatility constant. That is $M_t$ trend-stationary: $E[M_{t+s}\mid\mathcal F_t]=\rho^{s}M_t$, $0<\rho<1$, ${\rm Cov}(M_t,M_{t+s})=\gamma(s)$ constant in level. Then
  $E[X_{t+\Delta}\mid\mathcal F_t]=X_t+\mu\Delta+(\rho^{\Delta}-1)M_t$.
  The deviation is mean-reverting, $E[X_{t+\Delta}\mid\mathcal F_t]-X_t<\mu\Delta$ on $\{M_t>0\}$.
  With $V_h=\int T(t)d(-h_t)+\int M_t d(-h_t)$ a price-contingent rule can put sale weight on $M_t>0$ and less on $M_t<0$ and harvest the deviation before reversion erodes it. The Snell envelope on $[30,31]$ is strictly above the European payoff,
  $E[V_B^*]\ge E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_t^B]>E[P_{31}^B]=T(31)=V_A$,
  the strict inequality being $E[\sup M_t]>0$ for $\sigma>0$, i.e. the classic $E[\max X_t]>E[X_T]$ volatility/timing option value. Dominance is in mean only; pathwise $V_B^*$ can finish below $V_A$, so E and H are false and A is reverse.

The formal martingale statements B,C,D,F are false for price levels under the 10% physical drift; A is deterministic so F is false; B is a sub-martingale with drift so D is false. Pathwise necessity E,H remain false in either reading.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The first-moment comparison is settled by the predictable-integral decomposition, not by the ex-post supremum.

Write the 31st-year price in level form after removing the common 10% drift

$X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[M_{t}]=0,$

with $E[M_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=M_{s}$ for the drift-adjusted returns that the statement describes as stationary with constant autocovariance.  A is the $\sigma=0$ member of the same family, $P^{A}_{t}=T(t)$ a.s., so $V_{A}\equiv T(31)$ a.s.

Let $q_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction already sold on $[30,31]$, $dq_{t}\ge0$ predictable, $q_{30}=0$, $q_{31}=1$, and $C_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}X_{t}dq_{t}$.  Then

$C_{q}= \int_{30}^{31}T(t)dq_{t}+\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}dq_{t}$.

Integration by parts gives $\int M_{t}dq_{t}=M_{31}q_{31}-\int q_{t}dM_{t}$ and for every predictable $q$ $E\int q_{t}dM_{t}=0$. Hence

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}dq_{t}\right]=0$

for any causal, price-contingent sale plan. Consequently

$E[C_{q}]=\mu\,E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}t\,dq_{t}\right]
        =\mu\Bigl[31-E\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt\Bigr]\le\mu31,$

with equality iff $q_{t}\equiv0$ on $[30,31)$ and the whole position is sold at the terminal instant $T=31$. For a stopping time $\tau\le31$,

$E[X_{\tau}]=\mu E[\tau]+E[M_{\tau}]\le\mu31=E[X_{31}]$,

so the mean-maximising admissible liquidation is to hold to the very end of the admissible window.

That is why $E[P^{B}_{31}]=T(31)=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ and for every feasible adapted liquidation

$E[V_{B}^{*}]=E[X_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}$

in first moment. The $20\%$ weekly moves change dispersion only.

The inequality $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}X_{t}]>E[X_{31}]$ is true for the ex-post random variable $\sup_{t}X_{t}$, but $\sup_{t}X_{t}$ is not an attainable adapted payoff. The time of the overall intra-year maximum is not a stopping time that can be implemented by a predictable fractional sale rule that must end with $q_{31}=1$. Any rule that tries to “sell more when $Y_{t}>0$” necessarily shortens $E\int q_{t}dt$ and loses $\mu$-accrual; the stochastic integral against the zero-mean stationary part has zero unconditional mean.

Hence volatility raises risk and the second moment, it does not raise the unconditional expected liquidation value. The two baskets share the same $10\%$ p.a. average return and the same unconditional expected liquidation value under any feasible adapted liquidation. That is the economic content captured by C: stationary zero-mean detrended innovations give first-moment indifference of A and B, up to the usual drift-adjusted martingale shorthand for the price levels. Pathwise dominance E/H is false and the strict mean dominance claimed for G is the unattainable ex-post supremum fallacy.

4.text:
Basket A is degenerate on the physical measure

$P^{A}_{t}=P_{0}1.10^{t}$ a.s., so for every admissible liquidation in the

$V^{*}_{A}\equiv P_{0}1.10^{31}$ a.s. and the timing window is worthless
for A.  $P^{A}$ is not a martingale in price levels and F is false.

Write B on the common 10% trend as

$P^{B}_{t}=T(t)+Y_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[Y_{t}]=0,$

with the deviation $Y$ stationary with constant autocovariance,
$ {\rm Cov}(Y_{t},Y_{t+s})=\gamma(s)$,
and

$E[Y_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]=\rho^{\Delta}Y_{t},\qquad0<\rho<1,$

i.e. the “random walk around a mean with drift’’ described in the
statement.  Hence on a fixed calendar date

$E[P^{B}_{t}]=T(t)=E[P^{A}_{t}]$

and

$E[P^{B}_{t+\Delta}\mid{\cal F}_{t}]
 =T(t+\Delta)+\rho^{\Delta}Y_{t}
 =P^{B}_{t}+\mu\Delta+(\rho^{\Delta}-1)Y_{t}$.

and on $\{Y_{t}<0\}$ the inequality is reversed.  $P^{B}$ is therefore

stationary process.  The martingale prefaces in B,C,D are formally false
in price levels and D is false because B has the $10\%$ physical drift.

Then

intra-year realisations with $Y_{t}>0$ and less weight when $Y_{t}<0$.

reversion erodes it, $E[Y_{t+\Delta}\mid Y_{t}>0]<Y_{t}$.  In the limit

   >E[P^{B}_{31}]=T(31)=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}^{*},$

$\sigma_{Y}>0$.  With the $20\%$ weekly moves $\sigma_{Y}>0$ and the
free 31st-year liquidation is the classic American/timing option value
$E[\max X_{t}]>E[X_{T}]$.

does finish below $P^{A}$ so the pathwise necessity claims $E$ and $H$
are false and $A$ is the reverse ordering.  The price processes are
$10\%$ drifted, not physical martingales, so the formal martingale
statements B,C,D,F are false in the literal level sense and $A$ is
degenerate so $F$ is false.  The mean indifference $E[P^{B}_{31}]
=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ is the fixed-date European first moment; it is not the
expectation of the optimally adapted liquidation in the 31st year once
the constant-autocovariance trend-stationary deviation is allowed.

Hence under the stated trend-stationary, constant-autocovariance
reading the optimally liquidated volatile basket strictly dominates the
deterministic basket in unconditional mean, with no almost-sure ordering.

G. The strategy of choosing basket B has a higher expected value than
that of choosing basket A.

public_text.2:
The first-moment comparison is settled by the predictable-integral decomposition, not by the ex-post supremum.

Write the 31st-year price in level form after removing the common 10% drift

$X_{t}=T(t)+M_{t},\qquad T'(t)=\mu>0,\qquad E[M_{t}]=0,$

with $E[M_{t}\mid\mathcal F_{s}]=M_{s}$ for the drift-adjusted returns that the statement describes as stationary with constant autocovariance.  A is the $\sigma=0$ member of the same family, $P^{A}_{t}=T(t)$ a.s., so $V_{A}\equiv T(31)$ a.s.

Let $q_{t}\in[0,1]$ be the adapted fraction already sold on $[30,31]$, $dq_{t}\ge0$ predictable, $q_{30}=0$, $q_{31}=1$, and $C_{q}=\int_{30}^{31}X_{t}dq_{t}$.  Then

$C_{q}= \int_{30}^{31}T(t)dq_{t}+\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}dq_{t}$.

Integration by parts gives $\int M_{t}dq_{t}=M_{31}q_{31}-\int q_{t}dM_{t}$ and for every predictable $q$ $E\int q_{t}dM_{t}=0$. Hence

$E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}M_{t}dq_{t}\right]=0$

for any causal, price-contingent sale plan. Consequently

$E[C_{q}]=\mu\,E\!\left[\int_{30}^{31}t\,dq_{t}\right]
        =\mu\Bigl[31-E\int_{30}^{31}q_{t}dt\Bigr]\le\mu31,$

with equality iff $q_{t}\equiv0$ on $[30,31)$ and the whole position is sold at the terminal instant $T=31$. For a stopping time $\tau\le31$,

$E[X_{\tau}]=\mu E[\tau]+E[M_{\tau}]\le\mu31=E[X_{31}]$,

so the mean-maximising admissible liquidation is to hold to the very end of the admissible window.

That is why $E[P^{B}_{31}]=T(31)=E[P^{A}_{31}]$ and for every feasible adapted liquidation

$E[V_{B}^{*}]=E[X_{31}]=P_{0}1.10^{31}=V_{A}$

in first moment. The $20\%$ weekly moves change dispersion only.

The inequality $E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}X_{t}]>E[X_{31}]$ is true for the ex-post random variable $\sup_{t}X_{t}$, but $\sup_{t}X_{t}$ is not an attainable adapted payoff. The time of the overall intra-year maximum is not a stopping time that can be implemented by a predictable fractional sale rule that must end with $q_{31}=1$. Any rule that tries to “sell more when $Y_{t}>0$” necessarily shortens $E\int q_{t}dt$ and loses $\mu$-accrual; the stochastic integral against the zero-mean stationary part has zero unconditional mean.

Hence volatility raises risk and the second moment, it does not raise the unconditional expected liquidation value. The two baskets share the same $10\%$ p.a. average return and the same unconditional expected liquidation value under any feasible adapted liquidation. That is the economic content captured by C: stationary zero-mean detrended innovations give first-moment indifference of A and B, up to the usual drift-adjusted martingale shorthand for the price levels. Pathwise dominance E/H is false and the strict mean dominance claimed for G is the unattainable ex-post supremum fallacy.

G camp, trend-stationary / mean-reverting reading:

Then E[P^B_{t+Δ}|F_t]=P^B_t+μΔ+(ρ^Δ-1)Y_t < P^B_t+μΔ on {Y_t>0}. 
With adapted fraction h_t on [30,31], V_B(h)=∫ T(t)d(-h)+∫ Y_t d(-h). Mean reversion lets a price-contingent rule sell more when Y_t>0 and hold when Y_t<0, harvesting the transitory deviation before it reverts. In the limit the attainable mean is the Snell envelope,
E[V_B^*] ≥ E[sup_{30≤t≤31} P^B_t] > E[P^B_31]=T(31)=V_A,
strict for σ_Y>0 from the ±20% weekly moves. Dominance is in mean only; realised B can finish below A, so pathwise claims E,H false and reverse mean A false. Many colleagues 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18 present this derivation and conclude G is the only comparative mean statement in the list.

C camp, integrated martingale / difference-stationary reading:
P^B_t = T(t)+M_t with M zero-mean stationary increments, E[M_{t+s}|F_t]=M_t, i.e. returns stationary zero-mean, autocovariance of returns constant. For predictable q_t, ∫ M_t dq_t has zero unconditional mean by integration by parts, E[∫ q_t dM_t]=0. Hence
E[C_q]= μ E[∫ t dq_t]= μ[31-E∫ q_t dt] ≤ μ31,
with equality iff the position is held to the terminal instant 31. For any stopping time τ≤31, E[P^B_τ]=μE[τ]≤μ31=E[P^B_31]. reflection_text.6:
The first-moment comparison hinges on how “constant autocovariance + linear 10% trend + ARIMA with drift + random walk around a mean with drift’’ is read.

Basket A is degenerate: $P_t^A = P_0 1.10^t$ a.s., $V_A^* \equiv P_0 1.10^{31}$ a.s., timing in year 31 is worthless, $P^A$ is not a physical martingale and $F$ is false. Any almost-sure necessity $E,H$ is false.

For B the two camps disagree on the nature of the deviation about the trend.

G camp 1,10,11,12,15,16,17,18: write $P_t^B = T(t)+Y_t$, $T'(t)=\mu>0$, $E[Y_t]=0$, ${\rm Cov}(Y_t,Y_{t+s})=\gamma(s)$ constant, i.e. $Y$ trend-stationary, $E[Y_{t+\Delta}|{\cal F}_t]=\rho^\Delta Y_t$, $0<\rho<1$. Then
$E[P_{t+\Delta}^B|{\cal F}_t]=P_t^B+\mu\Delta+(\rho^\Delta-1)Y_t$.
A positive deviation is expected to mean-revert: $E[P_{t+\Delta}|{\cal F}_t] < P_t+\mu\Delta$ on $\{Y_t>0\}$.
With adapted holding $h_t$ on $[30,31]$
$V_B(h)=\int T d(-h)+\int Y d(-h)$,
a price-contingent rule that sells more when $Y_t>0$ and less when $Y_t<0$ makes $E\int Y d(-h)>0$.
The 31st year is an American look window and the Snell envelope satisfies
$E[V_B^*]\ge E[\sup_{30\le t\le31}P_t^B] > E[P_{31}^B]=T(31)=V_A^*$.
Strict $E[\max]>E[\text{terminal}]$ gives a volatility/timing option value; dominance is in mean only, no a.s. ordering. Under this reading $G$ is the only comparative mean statement that survives and B,C,D,F are formally false for price levels.

C camp 13,14,2,5,8,9: the ARIMA with drift clarification means stationary autocovariance is that of the returns / increments, not of the level deviation. Write $X_t=T(t)+M_t$, $E[M_t]=0$, $M_{t}-M_s$ stationary zero-mean. After detrending the innovations are a martingale difference. For predictable $q_t$ on $[30,31]$, $q_{30}=0,q_{31}=1$,
$C_q=\int T dq +\int M dq$,
$\int M dq = M_{31}q_{31}-\int q_t dM_t$, so $E\int M dq =0$.
Hence
$E[C_q]=\mu E\int t dq =\mu[31-E\int q_t dt]\le\mu31$,
with equality iff sell at $T=31$. For a stopping time $\tau\le31$,
$E[X_\tau]=\mu E[\tau]+E[M_\tau]\le\mu31=E[X_{31}]$.
Therefore $E[V_B^*]=E[P_{31}^B]=T(31)=P_0 1.10^{31}=V_A$ in first moment. 
$E[\sup X_t]>E[X_T]$ is true ex post, but $\sup_t X_t$ is not an attainable adapted payoff; the time of the overall intra-year maximum is not a stopping time and $E\int M dq =0$ for every predictable plan. Unresolved modeling tension persists: constant autocovariance of levels vs of returns, and whether “random walk around a mean with drift’’ means trend-stationary mean reversion or I(1) with drift. with equality iff the whole position is sold at the terminal instant. For a stopping time τ≤31, E[X_τ]=μE[τ]+E[M_τ]≤μ31=E[X_31]. The mean-maximising admissible causal liquidation is to hold to the very end of year 31. Hence
E[V_B*]=E[P^B_{31}]=P0 1.10^{31}=V_A
in first moment. E[sup X_t]>E[X_T] is true for the ex-post random variable sup_t X_t, but sup_t X_t is not an attainable adapted payoff; the time of the overall maximum is not a stopping time and no predictable fractional sale plan can replicate E[sup] in expectation. Volatility raises dispersion, not unconditional mean. Economic content is mean indifference, usually coded as C up to the loose martingale preface.

What remains unresolved:
* Whether “liquidated over the course of the 31st year with whatever liquidation strategy will maximise value’’ is read as an adapted predictable sale with E∫ M dq=0, i.e. the mean-indifference camp, or as a state-contingent intra-year harvesting of the trend-stationary deviation/Snell envelope that realises E[sup]>E[terminal], i.e. the G camp.
* The modelling of B: constant autocovariance of levels vs of returns. Constant autocovariance of levels implies trend-stationary mean-reversion ρ<1, supporting G; constant autocovariance of returns with an ARIMA(0,1,0) drift is a random walk with drift and martingale detrended increments, supporting mean-indifference. The statement “random walk around a mean with drift’’ is contradictory and is read differently by the two camps.
* Linear vs exponential reading of the 10% growth for A persists for exact form of V_A but does not affect ordering.

My current best summary retains both the optional-stopping mean-equality argument for admissible causal liquidations with a martingale detrended component and the convexity option-value argument for an ex-post supremum / mean-reverting deviation. Under strict predictability with a martingale detrended component the first-moment equality of the C camp holds; under the trend-stationary constant-autocovariance reading that the wording invokes, the mean dominance of G holds via the Snell envelope. Formal martingale statements B–F remain false for price levels, E and H remain false pathwise, and A is the reverse ordering.
